regulator: Colorado Department of Revenue (Marijuana Enforcement Division; Taxation Division)

data_source.name: Marijuana Sales Revenue in Colorado (Colorado Information Marketplace, dataset p6y8-s74x)
data_source.notes: Monthly retail (adult-use) and medical marijuana sales reported on Colorado Department of Revenue tax returns. Retail and medical are reported separately; the dataset's total is their sum. Sales figures exclude the taxes collected on them. Annual figures here are sums of the 12 official monthly rows.

annual.basis: sum of the official monthly figures
sum of the official monthly figures

tax_note: Adult-use (retail) marijuana carries a 15% state retail marijuana sales tax plus a 15% excise tax on the first wholesale transfer; medical marijuana pays the 2.9% state sales tax instead (Colorado Department of Revenue).
summary: Colorado opened the country's first adult-use stores in January 2014 and remains one of the largest markets, but sales have been drifting down. Licensed stores sold $111.2 million in July 2026, of which $102.1 million was adult-use. Combined sales were $1.40 billion in 2024 and $1.32 billion in 2025. The decline reflects falling wholesale and shelf prices, a shrinking medical program as patients move to adult-use stores, and competition from legal markets in neighboring states, especially New Mexico. Seasonal peaks still arrive in spring (around 4/20) and late summer, while February is typically the slowest month.

faq.q: How much cannabis does Colorado sell a month?
faq.a: In July 2026, Colorado's licensed stores sold $111.2 million of marijuana: $102.1 million adult-use and $9.1 million medical, according to Department of Revenue data.
No. Combined sales fell from $1.40 billion in 2024 to $1.32 billion in 2025, and 2026 months to date are running below the same months of 2025.

faq.q: Do Colorado's sales figures include tax?
faq.a: No. The Department of Revenue figures are sales reported on tax returns, before the 15% retail marijuana sales tax and other taxes are added.

faq.q: How big is Colorado's medical market?
faq.a: Medical sales were $9.1 million in July 2026, under a tenth of the total, and have been shrinking for years as patients shift to adult-use stores.
